Species richness of each site from a multispecies model

Source: R/fp_occu_ms-outputs.R
fp_richness.Rd

Counts, for each site, the species of an fp_occu_ms() model that are present, from the posterior of the occupancy state of every species at the site. In development, as fp_occu_ms().

Usage

fp_richness(object, prob = 0.95, ndraws = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

object

An fp_occu_ms object.

prob

Width of the credible intervals.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws to use (all by default).

seed

Optional seed for the choice of draws.

Value

A data frame, one row per site, with the site columns of the data, richness (posterior mean number of species present, with richness_lower and richness_upper, quantiles of its posterior distribution), richness_psi (expected number of species from the occupancy covariates alone, before the data of the site), detected (number of species with automated detections) and verified (number of species whose presence a verified detection proves).

Details

For each posterior draw, the state of each species at each site is drawn from its conditional posterior given the data of that species at that site (as in fp_sites()), and the richness of the site is the number of species drawn as present. The species are those of the model: a species never detected anywhere is not in the list and is not counted.

See also

fp_occu_ms(), fp_sites()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s <- simulate_fp_ms(nspecies = 5, nsite = 60, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu_ms(s$data, occ = ~ x, det = ~ bio, random_recorder = FALSE)
r <- fp_richness(m)
plot(rowSums(s$truth$z), r$richness)
} # }
